actual_request.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce ONE newly drawn genuine walking animation frame for the exact same chibi Daoist calligrapher boy. Reference 1 is the approved N rear-facing idle: lock its identity, rear costume construction, hand assignment, giant brush and scroll shapes, head/body proportions, subject scale, camera, and drawing detail. Reference 2 shows original identity from front; reference 3 gives the approved polished Chinese fantasy illustration style only. This frame faces due NORTH straight away from camera, back fully visible, no face. Anatomical RIGHT hand/image-right holds giant black-jade-gold calligraphy brush with downward white bristles; anatomical LEFT hand/image-left holds the hanging pale scroll with black-gold rollers and two little pale blue spirit companions. Brown tousled topknot, teal ribbon, warm black robe with gold cloud borders, white inner robe, teal lining and belt, black-gold boots. The round yin-yang head badge and belt buckle belong on the FRONT and remain hidden from the rear: no face or forehead mark or front buckle on back.
Camera and framing MUST match approved reference 1 exactly: mild top-down orthographic game view, complete figure centered, square canvas minimum 1024x1024 native, top of hair near y=7%, lowest planted foot near y=94%, generous side margins. Draw real anatomy, both separate feet visible below robe, not running or jumping, at least one grounded support foot. Keep prop motion small and scale stable. Transparent PNG actual alpha, no floor or cast shadow, no colored outline, no labels/text/grid. One complete single pose only. Do not use mirror, interpolation, distortion, duplication or translation of another pose.
WALK N FRAME 08/16. 43.75% PRE-CONTACT: LEFT leg nearly fully reached forward, heel just above ground about to contact; RIGHT leg trails with forefoot still grounded and heel high. Body eases down into next contact, leg separation clear, no flight phase. One frame before opposite contact. In REAR view anatomical right is image-right, anatomical left is image-left. Farther-forward foot projects higher on image; trailing foot projects lower. Preserve all upper-body and equipment identity features. Draw this unique phase specifically.
